checked_claims.claim: residplot participates in bootstrap regression confidence intervals
checked_claims.reason: residplot explicitly sets ci=None; fast bootstrap returns coefficients then projects to predictions.

material_errors: residplot explicitly sets ci=None; fast bootstrap returns coefficients then projects to predictions.
tasks.notes: Source review, no execution or timing performed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: regplot constructs a regression plotter whose fit_regression dispatches model-specific fitting and uses utils.ci(yhat_boots, ci, axis=0) for bands (seaborn/regression.py:188-227). For fast linear fitting, bootstrap resamples X/y to estimate coefficients, then grid.dot converts them to prediction samples (seaborn/regression.py:229-245). algorithms.bootstrap resamples rows jointly or delegates unit resampling (seaborn/algorithms.py:91-120). residplot sets ci=None and does not produce these bootstrap confidence bands (seaborn/regression.py:905-915); LOWESS also disables them.

checked_claims.reason: Legacy refits KDE per evaluation even when support cached; newer transform shares computed support across grouped fits. Evolution rationale is inferred.

tasks.notes: Source review, no execution or timing performed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Legacy KDE.define_support can store an evaluation grid, but _eval_univariate still fits a KDE each evaluation (seaborn/_statistics.py:124-163). Modern KDE computes support in _transform then passes it to grouped fits, with common_grid controlling sharing (seaborn/_stats/density.py:157-194). Thus these are different grid-lifetime designs for different plotting interfaces, not caching versus recomputing all statistical work. Source does not establish the asserted performance-driven retention rationale.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Plot._plot coordinates extraction, figure setup, coordinate scales, statistics, another scale pass, then per-layer drawing (seaborn/_core/plot.py:920-952). _compute_stats calls the Stat object as stat(df, groupby, orient, scales), invoking __call__ (seaborn/_core/plot.py:1230-1235). _plot_layer likewise calls each Move object, unscales coordinates, builds the split generator and invokes mark._plot (seaborn/_core/plot.py:1456-1474). The interfaces are __call__, not Stat.call or Move.call.
